until_next_occurrence.description: Allow late submission until the next occurrence starts.

late_submission_duration.description:
Allow late submission for a specific duration after each occurrence ends.
Currently only supports a period of 14 days ("P14D"). ISO 8601 duration format.

s12.scheduling.v1.LateSubmissionRule.description: The conditions under which users can submit work late for each occurrence.

dtstart_rrule.title:
Supported RRULE frequencies and intervals:
- WEEKLY: BYDAY with multiple weekdays (e.g., BYDAY=MO,WE,FR)
- MONTHLY: BYMONTHDAY=1-28 OR BYSETPOS=1-4,-1 with BYDAY (single weekday)
- YEARLY: BYMONTH (required) with either BYMONTHDAY or BYSETPOS+BYDAY

duration.description: Duration in ISO 8601 format (e.g., "PT1H"). Defines the window from start to due.

use_site_timezone.description:
When true, use each target site's timezone instead of the RRULE timezone.
Only applicable when target is sites or assets (uses the asset's parent site timezone).
When enabled, any timezone specified in the RRULE will be ignored and set to the default time, UTC.

late_submission_rule.description:
The conditions under which users can submit work late for each occurrence.
When not set, late submission is not allowed.

s12.scheduling.v1.ScheduleRecurrence.description:
ScheduleRecurrence defines when and how often the schedule repeats.

RFC 5545 recurrence definition combining DTSTART and RRULE properties.
 DTSTART specifies the start time and timezone. RRULE defines the recurrence pattern.
 Timezone defaults to UTC if unspecified, or if `use_site_timezone` is true.

 Expected format: "DTSTART;TZID=America/New_York:20240101T140000\nRRULE:FREQ=DAILY;INTERVAL=1"

recurrence.description:
The new recurrence configuration for the schedule.
Replaces all existing recurrence fields, including the recurrence pattern,
duration, timezone, and late submission rule.

effective_from.description: Controls when the recurrence changes take effect on sub-schedules.

s12.scheduling.v1.SchedulingService.Upda.description: UpdateScheduleRecurrence replaces the recurrence configuration for an existing schedule.

s12.scheduling.v1.UntilNextOccurrence.description:
UntilNextOccurrence indicates late submission is allowed until the next occurrence starts.
Used as a marker type in oneof fields.

s12.scheduling.v1.UpdateEffectiveFrom.description:
UpdateEffectiveFrom specifies when schedule changes should take effect.

 - UPDATE_EFFECTIVE_FROM_UNSPECIFIED: Unspecified.
 - UPDATE_EFFECTIVE_FROM_CURRENT_OCCURRENCE: Apply changes starting from the current occurrence.
 - UPDATE_EFFECTIVE_FROM_NEXT_OCCURRENCE: Apply changes starting from the next occurrence.

patch.description: Replaces the assignment rule for a schedule. The selected option replaces the current assignees entirely. Use 'users' to assign specific users, 'groups' to assign all members of a group, 'site_members' to assign all members of the target site(s), or 'site_members_in_group' to assign site members who are also in a group. The site_members and site_members_in_group options require the schedule to have targets (sites or assets) set.

parameters.name: schedule_id
parameters.description: ID of the schedule to update.

oneOf.title: Group
oneOf.description: Assign all members of the specified group. Replaces any current assignment with group-based assignment.

oneOf.title: Site Members
oneOf.description: Assign all members of the target site(s). Requires the schedule to have targets (sites or assets) set.

site_members.description:
UpdateSiteMemberAssignment changes the schedule to assign to all members of the target site(s).

The schedule must have targets (sites or assets) set for this option to work.

oneOf.title: Site Members in Group
oneOf.description: Assign site members who are also in the specified group (intersection). Requires the schedule to have targets (sites or assets) set.

group_ids.description:
Group IDs to assign. Currently supports only one group.
Replaces any existing assignment strategy.

s12.scheduling.v1.UpdateGroupAssignment.description: UpdateGroupAssignment changes the schedule to assign to all members of a group.

group_ids.description: Group IDs for intersection filtering. Currently supports only one group.

s12.scheduling.v1.UpdateSiteMemberInGrou.description:
UpdateSiteMemberInGroupAssignment changes the schedule to assign to site members
who are also in the specified group (intersection).

The schedule must have targets (sites or assets) set for this option to work.

user_ids.description:
User IDs to assign.
Replaces any existing assignees with this list.

s12.scheduling.v1.UpdateUserAssignees.description: UpdateUserAssignees modifies the list of specifically assigned users.

externalDocs.description: How to generate an API Token

@type.description:
A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized
protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least
one "/" character. The last segment of the URL's path must represent
the fully qualified name of the type (as in
`path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form
(e.g., leading "." is not accepted).

In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they
expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the
scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type
server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:

* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed.
* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a [google.protobuf.Type][]
  value in binary format, or produce an error.
* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the
  URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any
  lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved
  on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage
  breaking changes.)

Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official
protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with
type.googleapis.com.

Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be
used with implementation specific semantics.

FieldValue represents a single field and its value within a structure profile.

field_name.description: The display name for the field.

value_type.description: The type of value stored in this field.

created_at.description: The timestamp when this field value was created.

created_by.description: The user ID of the user who created this field value.

is_default_value.description: Indicates whether this field value is the default value for the field.

is_field_required.description: Indicates whether this field is required for the structure type.

FieldValueInput is the input message for setting a field value.

which is useful for historical accuracy and API convenience.

This is used for fields where exactly one option can be selected from a predefined list.

s12.structures.v1.StatusType.description:
- STATUS_TYPE_ACTIVE: The structure is active and can be used.
 - STATUS_TYPE_PENDING: The structure has been created but is not yet active.
 - STATUS_TYPE_DELETED: The structure has been deleted.

id.description: Unique identifier for the structure

creator_id.description: The user id responsible for creating the structure

created_at.description: The creation timestamp of the structure

modified_at.description: The timestamp of the last modification for the structure

deleted_at.description: The timestamp of the structure deletion

is_dynamic.description:
Whether the structure's membership is calculated by a rule rather than
assigned directly.

description.description: Free-text description of the structure. Empty if none is set.

ancestors.description: Ancestors of Structure. List Ordered by Structure depth descending

is_hierarchical.description: Whether this structure type supports hierarchical relationships (can have parent/children structures)

can_move.description:
Whether this structure can be moved to a different parent. Structures of a
type that does not support hierarchy cannot be moved.

meta_label.description:
The hierarchical classification of this structure (e.g. "location", "area", "region", "state", "country").
Derived by the backend based on the structure's position in the hierarchy — read-only.

fields.description: Fields on Structure. Fields are shown only where "Show On Profile" Setting is True

direct_member_count.description:
The number of users assigned directly to this structure, excluding users
who inherit membership from an ancestor.

id.description: ID of the Ancestor belonging to the Structure.

depth.description: Depth relative to the Structure. Structure self depth = 0. Direct parent depth = 1.

postal_code.description: The postal code of the location.

iso_country_code.description: The ISO country code of the location.

geo_position.description: The geographic position of the location.

phone.description: The phone number of the contact.

email.description: The email address of the contact.

s12.typefield.v1.ContactDetails.description: Contact details for a person or entity.

id.description: The id of a field select option.

label.description: The label of a field select option.

order.description:
The display order of this option, 0-indexed.
Options should be displayed in ascending order of this field,

 - FIELD_VALUE_TYPE_CONTACT_DETAILS: Field value type contact details

get.description: Returns the core metadata for a structure: its name, type, status, creator and timestamps. Use this instead of the full structure endpoint when you do not need ancestors or field values. Pass `field_mask` to restrict which metadata fields are populated.

parameters.name: structure_id
parameters.description: Required. The unique identifier of the structure.

parameters.name: field_mask
parameters.description: Optional. Controls which fields of the StructureMetadata are populated in the response.

@type.description:
A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized
protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least
one "/" character. The last segment of the URL's path must represent
the fully qualified name of the type (as in
`path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form
(e.g., leading "." is not accepted).

In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they
expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the
scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type
server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:

* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed.
* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a [google.protobuf.Type][]
  value in binary format, or produce an error.
* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the
  URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any
  lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved
  on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage
  breaking changes.)

Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official
protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with
type.googleapis.com.

Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be
used with implementation specific semantics.

s12.common.GeoPosition.description: A position is the fundamental geographical geometry construct.

query.description: Search query matched against structure content. May be empty.

filters.description: Optional. Filters to apply to the result set.

include_matches.description:
Optional. If true, each result includes the field key/value pairs
that matched the query (useful for highlighting). Off by default.

include_fields.description:
Optional. If true, each result is returned with its fully-populated
field values (see StructureSearchResult.fields). Off by default, as it
adds field-name resolution on top of the search. Independent of
include_matches, which only reports the fields that matched the query.

is_dynamic.description:
Optional. Only return structures with this is_dynamic value.
Unset returns both dynamic and non-dynamic.

structure_uuids.description:
Optional. Restrict to these structure UUIDs (OR-combined).
api-directory forwards a restricted caller's entire visible-site scope in
this field when scoping SearchStructures, so the cap must exceed the largest
visible scope (tens of thousands) while staying under OpenSearch's default
65,536 terms-query limit.

field_values.description:
Optional. Restrict to structures whose field values match these
filters. OR within a filter, AND across filters.

s12.search.v1.StructureSearchParams.Filt.description: Filters narrow which structures are returned.

values.description:
Each entry is an exact-value predicate. Prefer `matches`, which
supersedes this field; `values` is retained for callers that have not
migrated and will be marked deprecated once `matches` is no longer
experimental.

s12.search.v1.StructureSearchParams.Filt.description:
A single field plus the values it may match. Values within one
filter are OR-combined; multiple filters are AND-combined.

page_size.description: Results per page. Default 20. Maximum 100.

page_token.description: Token for retrieving the next page of results. Absent on the first page.

structure_type.description: Structure type identifier (e.g. "folder", "site"). Empty if not categorized.

created_at.description: When the structure was created.

updated_at.description: When the structure was last modified.

similarity_score.description: Relevance score, 0.0–1.0. Higher is more relevant.

parent.description: Parent of the matched structure. Unset for root structures.

matches.description:
Fields that matched the query. Only populated when the request set
include_matches = true.

is_dynamic.description: True if membership is governed by a rule rather than explicit assignment.

description.description: Free-text description of the structure. Empty if none is set.

fields.description:
Fully-populated field values for the structure. Only populated when the
request set include_fields = true. Field display names (field_name) are
resolved to their current values at query time, so they stay correct even
if the field was renamed after the structure was last indexed.

ancestors.description:
Full ancestor chain from root to direct parent, in order. Empty for root
structures and for non-hierarchical (Group) results. Additive to `parent`.

s12.search.v1.StructureSearchResult.description: A single structure that matched the search query.

name.description:
Display name of the ancestor structure. Empty when masked or
unresolved for the caller.

label.description:
Hierarchical label of the ancestor structure (e.g. "region",
"country", "state").

direct_member_count.description:
Number of direct members of the ancestor structure. Matches the type
of the outer StructureSearchResult.direct_member_count.

s12.search.v1.StructureSearchResult.Ance.description: Ancestor of the matched structure, from root down to the direct parent.

key.description: Field name (e.g. "address", or a custom field id).

value.description: Field value containing the matched substring.

field_id.description:
Field identifier for filter-derived matches. `key` may be empty for
such matches (e.g. optional custom fields), so clients should resolve
the display name from their own field definitions using this id.

s12.search.v1.StructureSearchResult.Matc.description:
A field whose value matched the query. Useful for highlighting on
the client. The structure's name is not included — it's already at
the top level.

name.description: Display name of the parent structure.

s12.structures.types.v1.FieldValueData.description:
FieldValueData contains the typed value stored for a field, without field metadata such as
field ID, name, timestamps, or requirement/default information.

Intended to become the canonical FieldValueData across the API. For now the
wire-compatible original still lives at s12.structures.v1.FieldValueData to avoid
breaking existing consumers; that copy should be removed once callers have migrated.

string_value.description: String value for FIELD_VALUE_TYPE_STRING, FIELD_VALUE_TYPE_TIMEZONE, FIELD_VALUE_TYPE_USER_ID, FIELD_VALUE_TYPE_TEMPLATE_ID and FIELD_VALUE_TYPE_SITE.

timestamp_value.description: Timestamp value for FIELD_VALUE_TYPE_TIMESTAMP.

reference_value.description:
Reference value carrying both the raw id (the filter key) and an optional
resolved display label, for the reference field types FIELD_VALUE_TYPE_USER_ID,
FIELD_VALUE_TYPE_SITE and FIELD_VALUE_TYPE_TEMPLATE_ID. Used where a service
can resolve a human-readable label (e.g. ListUniqueFieldValues); the bare
string_value above is still used where no label is available.

id.description:
The referenced entity's id. This is the filter key — pass it back as a
string_value in SearchStructuresRequest.params.filters.field_values[].values
to filter on this value.

label.description:
Human-readable label for the referenced entity (e.g. a user's display name).
Display-only. Unset when the referent is deleted or inaccessible to the
caller; clients should fall back to the id in that case.

s12.structures.types.v1.ReferenceValue.description:
ReferenceValue is the value of a reference field (user, site, template) paired
with an optional resolved display label.

selected_option_id.description:
The ID of the selected option.
This references a FieldOption defined in the associated field type.

options.description:
The list of available options for this field.
This provides a snapshot of the options available at the time the value was set,
which is useful for historical accuracy and API convenience.

s12.structures.types.v1.SingleSelectValu.description:
SingleSelectValue represents a single-select field value.
This is used for fields where exactly one option can be selected from a predefined list.

Intended to become the canonical SingleSelectValue across the API. For now the
wire-compatible original still lives at s12.structures.v1.SingleSelectValue to avoid
breaking existing consumers; that copy should be removed once callers have migrated.

field_id.description: The unique identifier of the field type definition.

field_name.description:
The field's display name. Producers that read from a denormalized store
(e.g. a search index) should resolve this to its current value, as the
stored copy may be stale. May be empty if the field can no longer be
resolved.

value_type.description: The type of value stored in this field.

value.description: The typed value stored for the field.

is_default_value.description:
True if this value is the field's default value rather than one set
explicitly on the structure.

is_field_required.description: True if this field is required for the structure's type.

s12.structures.types.v1.StructureFieldVa.description:
StructureFieldValue is one fully-populated field on a structure, pairing the
field's metadata (id, display name, value type) with its typed value. It is
the canonical metadata-carrying counterpart to FieldValueData (which holds the
value only).

s12.structures.types.v1.StructureTypeIde.description:
Identifies a single structure type, either by built-in system type or
by org-defined UUID. Use in place of a bare structure_type_id string
when callers may want to reference well-known types without resolving
the org's UUID.

system_structure_type.description:
Built-in system type — convenient shorthand so clients don't need
to resolve the org's UUID for well-known types.

structure_type_id.description: UUID of an org-defined structure type.

s12.structures.types.v1.SystemStructureT.description:
Built-in structure types that exist across every organization without
needing an org-defined UUID. Use SystemStructureType when referring to
these well-known types by name.

structure_type.description:
Required. Restricts the search to structures of this type. Either a
built-in system type or an org-defined structure type UUID.

s12.structures.v1.SearchStructuresReques.description: Request for SearchStructures. Organization is taken from the caller's auth.

next_page_token.description: Token for the next page. Empty on the last page.

total_count.description:
Total number of matching structures across all pages. Accurate up to
10,000; beyond that it is a lower bound (treat a value of 10000 as
"10,000+").

put.description: Replaces a structure's name, description and field values. This is a full replacement, not a partial update: an omitted `description` is cleared, and any field value that is not present in `fields` is cleared. Send the structure's complete field set on every request.

parameters.description: The identifier of the structure to update

structure_id.description: The unique identifier of the structure.

role_id.description: The unique identifier of the role assigned to the user within the structure.

created_at.description: The timestamp when the user was added to the structure.

modified_at.description: The timestamp when the membership was last modified.

assignment_type.description:
How this membership was assigned: explicitly by a user, or computed by a

s12.structures.membership.v1.StructureMe.description: StructureMembership represents a user's membership within a structure, including their assigned role.

AssignmentType classifies how this membership was assigned: explicitly

 - ASSIGNMENT_TYPE_MANUAL: The membership was explicitly assigned by a user.
 - ASSIGNMENT_TYPE_RULE_BASED: The membership was computed by a dynamic-structure rule.

user_ids.description: The unique identifiers of the users to add. Limited to 100 users per request.

s12.structures.membership.v1.StructureMe.description: Request message to add one or more users to a structure.

post.description: Removes up to 100 users from a structure. Only direct memberships are removed — a user who inherits membership from an ancestor structure keeps that inherited membership. This endpoint supports partial success: a user who could not be removed is reported in `errors` with a status code and a reason, and a response with a populated `errors` array is still a 200. A rule-based membership is reported this way rather than removed, because only a change to the rule can remove it.

currency_code.description: The 3-letter currency code defined in ISO 4217.

units.description:
The whole units of the amount.
For example if `currencyCode` is `"USD"`, then 1 unit is one US dollar.

nanos.description:
Number of nano (10^-9) units of the amount.
The value must be between -999,999,999 and +999,999,999 inclusive.
If `units` is positive, `nanos` must be positive or zero.
If `units` is zero, `nanos` can be positive, zero, or negative.
If `units` is negative, `nanos` must be negative or zero.
For example £-1.75 is represented as `units`=-1 and `nanos`=-750,000,000.

@type.description:
A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized
protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least
one "/" character. The last segment of the URL's path must represent
the fully qualified name of the type (as in
`path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form
(e.g., leading "." is not accepted).

In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they
expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the
scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type
server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:

* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed.
* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a [google.protobuf.Type][]
  value in binary format, or produce an error.
* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the
  URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any
  lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved
  on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage
  breaking changes.)

Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official
protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with
type.googleapis.com.

Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be
used with implementation specific semantics.

currency_code.description: The 3-letter currency code defined in ISO 4217.

units.description:
The whole units of the amount.
For example if `currencyCode` is `"USD"`, then 1 unit is one US dollar.

nanos.description:
Number of nano (10^-9) units of the amount.
The value must be between -999,999,999 and +999,999,999 inclusive.
If `units` is positive, `nanos` must be positive or zero.
If `units` is zero, `nanos` can be positive, zero, or negative.
If `units` is negative, `nanos` must be negative or zero.
For example £-1.75 is represented as `units`=-1 and `nanos`=-750,000,000.

@type.description:
A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized
protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least
one "/" character. The last segment of the URL's path must represent
the fully qualified name of the type (as in
`path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form
(e.g., leading "." is not accepted).

In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they
expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the
scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type
server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:

* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed.
* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a [google.protobuf.Type][]
  value in binary format, or produce an error.
* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the
  URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any
  lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved
  on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage
  breaking changes.)

Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official
protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with
type.googleapis.com.

Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be
used with implementation specific semantics.

currency_code.description: The 3-letter currency code defined in ISO 4217.

units.description:
The whole units of the amount.
For example if `currencyCode` is `"USD"`, then 1 unit is one US dollar.

nanos.description:
Number of nano (10^-9) units of the amount.
The value must be between -999,999,999 and +999,999,999 inclusive.
If `units` is positive, `nanos` must be positive or zero.
If `units` is zero, `nanos` can be positive, zero, or negative.
If `units` is negative, `nanos` must be negative or zero.
For example £-1.75 is represented as `units`=-1 and `nanos`=-750,000,000.

currency_code.description: The 3-letter currency code defined in ISO 4217.

units.description:
The whole units of the amount.
For example if `currencyCode` is `"USD"`, then 1 unit is one US dollar.

nanos.description:
Number of nano (10^-9) units of the amount.
The value must be between -999,999,999 and +999,999,999 inclusive.
If `units` is positive, `nanos` must be positive or zero.
If `units` is zero, `nanos` can be positive, zero, or negative.
If `units` is negative, `nanos` must be negative or zero.
For example £-1.75 is represented as `units`=-1 and `nanos`=-750,000,000.

@type.description:
A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized
protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least
one "/" character. The last segment of the URL's path must represent
the fully qualified name of the type (as in
`path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form
(e.g., leading "." is not accepted).

In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they
expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the
scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type
server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:

* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed.
* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a [google.protobuf.Type][]
  value in binary format, or produce an error.
* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the
  URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any
  lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved
  on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage
  breaking changes.)

Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official
protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with
type.googleapis.com.

Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be
used with implementation specific semantics.

currency_code.description: The 3-letter currency code defined in ISO 4217.

units.description:
The whole units of the amount.
For example if `currencyCode` is `"USD"`, then 1 unit is one US dollar.

nanos.description:
Number of nano (10^-9) units of the amount.
The value must be between -999,999,999 and +999,999,999 inclusive.
If `units` is positive, `nanos` must be positive or zero.
If `units` is zero, `nanos` can be positive, zero, or negative.
If `units` is negative, `nanos` must be negative or zero.
For example £-1.75 is represented as `units`=-1 and `nanos`=-750,000,000.

ai_edited.description:
True when something non deterministic, in practice an LLM, produced or
changed this content. False when no AI did, which includes content a person
wrote and content a deterministic path produced. Absent when the origin was
not recorded. Do not report false in place of absent.

human_edited.description:
True when a person authored or changed this content. False when no person
did, which includes content a model generated and content a deterministic
path produced. Absent when the origin was not recorded. Do not report false
in place of absent.

s12.common.v1.AiMarking.description:
AiMarking carries the AI marking fact on an API representation, so a machine
can read whether AI and whether a person produced or changed the content.
It is the read side of the express path: one shared message with standard
property names, rather than every domain inventing its own field for the
same fact.

Both fields are presence tracked. The three states each carry a different
meaning and must not be collapsed:

  true    The actor named by the field produced or changed this content.
  false   The actor named by the field is known not to have produced or
          changed this content. It is a claim about that actor only.
  absent  We did not record the origin.

false is not evidence that a deterministic path produced the content. Known
human only content can read ai_edited false, and known AI only content can
read human_edited false. Set a field to false only when you know it is false.
Leave it absent when you do not, so a consumer relying on the API for their
own obligation can tell "not true" from "not recorded". EU AI Act Article
50(2), engineering approach page.

description.description: Optional. Description of the issue (maximum 500 characters).

The collaborators involved in this issue.
Collaborators are users who have been assigned to the issue. The user will
appear in the "Assignee" field in the issue. Only one user can be assigned
to an issue at a time.

If not set, this issue will be stored with the default status (Open).
An issue can be open, in progress, or resolved, and these are represented
by hardcoded UUID values. Open status: `547ed646-5e34-4732-bb54-a199d304368a`.
In Progress status: `ca6f3bc7-b943-406e-8399-8a713b7e6268`.
Resolved status: `450484b1-56cd-4784-9b49-a3cf97d0c0ad`.

ai_edited.description:
True when something non deterministic, in practice an LLM, produced or
changed this content. False when no AI did, which includes content a person
wrote and content a deterministic path produced. Absent when the origin was
not recorded. Do not report false in place of absent.

human_edited.description:
True when a person authored or changed this content. False when no person
did, which includes content a model generated and content a deterministic
path produced. Absent when the origin was not recorded. Do not report false
in place of absent.

s12.common.v1.AiMarking.description:
AiMarking carries the AI marking fact on an API representation, so a machine
can read whether AI and whether a person produced or changed the content.
It is the read side of the express path: one shared message with standard
property names, rather than every domain inventing its own field for the
same fact.

Both fields are presence tracked. The three states each carry a different
meaning and must not be collapsed:

  true    The actor named by the field produced or changed this content.
  false   The actor named by the field is known not to have produced or
          changed this content. It is a claim about that actor only.
  absent  We did not record the origin.

false is not evidence that a deterministic path produced the content. Known
human only content can read ai_edited false, and known AI only content can
read human_edited false. Set a field to false only when you know it is false.
Leave it absent when you do not, so a consumer relying on the API for their
own obligation can tell "not true" from "not recorded". EU AI Act Article
50(2), engineering approach page.

CategoryNotificationDetail represents the different level of detail for category notifications.

 - CATEGORY_NOTIFICATION_DETAIL_UNSPECIFIED: CATEGORY_NOTIFICATION_DETAIL_UNSPECIFIED is the default value and should not be used.
 - CATEGORY_NOTIFICATION_DETAIL_PRIVATE: CATEGORY_NOTIFICATION_DETAIL_PRIVATE notifications will be restricted to public metadata.
 - CATEGORY_NOTIFICATION_DETAIL_SUMMARY: CATEGORY_NOTIFICATION_DETAIL_SUMMARY notifications will include public and private metadata.
 - CATEGORY_NOTIFICATION_DETAIL_FULL: CATEGORY_NOTIFICATION_DETAIL_FULL will include all metadata and detailed responses.

 - CATEGORY_USER_ACCESS_AS_REPORTER_NEVER: CATEGORY_USER_ACCESS_AS_REPORTER_NEVER the user will never gain access to issues they report
 - CATEGORY_USER_ACCESS_AS_REPORTER_WHEN_SITE_MEMBER: CATEGORY_USER_ACCESS_AS_REPORTER_WHEN_SITE_MEMBER the user will gain access to issues they report
when they have membership to the site that the issue has been raised at

s12.tasks.v1.GetIncidentsRequest.SortDir.description:
The options available to define the sort direction.

 - SORT_DIRECTION_UNKNOWN: `SORT_DIRECTION_UNKNOWN` will return the default sort direction.
 - ASC: `ASC` will return the sorted issues in ascending order.
 - DESC: `DESC` will return the sorted issues in descending order.

s12.tasks.v1.GetIncidentsRequest.SortFie.description:
The options available to sort the issues by.
By default, the issues will be returned by the date they were last
modified in descending order. This should be used in combination with
`SortDirection` to determine how issues are sorted. If either
`SortField` or `SortDirection` is missing, the default sort order will be
used.

 - SORT_FIELD_UNKNOWN: `SORT_FIELD_UNKNOWN` will return the default sort order.
 - PRIORITY: `PRIORITY` will sort the issues by incident priority.
 - DATE_DUE: `DATE_DUE` will sort the issues by due date.
 - CREATED_AT: `CREATED_AT` will sort the issues by the date they were created.
 - MODIFIED_AT: `MODIFIED_AT` will sort the issues by the date they were last
modified.
 - OCCURRED_AT: `OCCURRED_AT` will sort the issues by the date they occurred at.

externalDocs.description: How to generate an API Token

@type.description:
A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized
protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least
one "/" character. The last segment of the URL's path must represent
the fully qualified name of the type (as in
`path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form
(e.g., leading "." is not accepted).

In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they
expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the
scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type
server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:

* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed.
* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a [google.protobuf.Type][]
  value in binary format, or produce an error.
* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the
  URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any
  lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved
  on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage
  breaking changes.)

Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official
protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with
type.googleapis.com.

Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be
used with implementation specific semantics.

s12.tasks.v1.GetIncidentsRequest.SortDir.description:
The options available to define the sort direction.

 - SORT_DIRECTION_UNKNOWN: `SORT_DIRECTION_UNKNOWN` will return the default sort direction.
 - ASC: `ASC` will return the sorted issues in ascending order.
 - DESC: `DESC` will return the sorted issues in descending order.

s12.tasks.v1.GetIncidentsRequest.SortFie.description:
The options available to sort the issues by.
By default, the issues will be returned by the date they were last
modified in descending order. This should be used in combination with
`SortDirection` to determine how issues are sorted. If either
`SortField` or `SortDirection` is missing, the default sort order will be
used.

 - SORT_FIELD_UNKNOWN: `SORT_FIELD_UNKNOWN` will return the default sort order.
 - PRIORITY: `PRIORITY` will sort the issues by incident priority.
 - DATE_DUE: `DATE_DUE` will sort the issues by due date.
 - CREATED_AT: `CREATED_AT` will sort the issues by the date they were created.
 - MODIFIED_AT: `MODIFIED_AT` will sort the issues by the date they were last
modified.
 - OCCURRED_AT: `OCCURRED_AT` will sort the issues by the date they occurred at.

@type.description:
A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized
protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least
one "/" character. The last segment of the URL's path must represent
the fully qualified name of the type (as in
`path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form
(e.g., leading "." is not accepted).

In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they
expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the
scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type
server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:

* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed.
* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a [google.protobuf.Type][]
  value in binary format, or produce an error.
* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the
  URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any
  lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved
  on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage
  breaking changes.)

Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official
protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with
type.googleapis.com.

Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be
used with implementation specific semantics.

ai_edited.description:
True when something non deterministic, in practice an LLM, produced or
changed this content. False when no AI did, which includes content a person
wrote and content a deterministic path produced. Absent when the origin was
not recorded. Do not report false in place of absent.

human_edited.description:
True when a person authored or changed this content. False when no person
did, which includes content a model generated and content a deterministic
path produced. Absent when the origin was not recorded. Do not report false
in place of absent.

s12.common.v1.AiMarking.description:
AiMarking carries the AI marking fact on an API representation, so a machine
can read whether AI and whether a person produced or changed the content.
It is the read side of the express path: one shared message with standard
property names, rather than every domain inventing its own field for the
same fact.

Both fields are presence tracked. The three states each carry a different
meaning and must not be collapsed:

  true    The actor named by the field produced or changed this content.
  false   The actor named by the field is known not to have produced or
          changed this content. It is a claim about that actor only.
  absent  We did not record the origin.

false is not evidence that a deterministic path produced the content. Known
human only content can read ai_edited false, and known AI only content can
read human_edited false. Set a field to false only when you know it is false.
Leave it absent when you do not, so a consumer relying on the API for their
own obligation can tell "not true" from "not recorded". EU AI Act Article
50(2), engineering approach page.

- TEMPERATURE: Temperature metric
 - HUMIDITY: Humidity metric
 - BATTERY: Battery level. Percentage based i.e. 0 - 100

 - AIR_QUALITY_PM25: Air quality for particulate matter less than 2.5 microns
 - AIR_QUALITY_PM10: Air quality for particulate matter less than 10 microns
 - TEMPERATURE_2: Alternative temperature (Some hardware i.e. Avem Quirks do have 2 probes
and are sending 2 temperatures)
 - DIFFERENTIAL_AIR_PRESSURE: Differential air pressure
 - CO: Carbon monoxide
 - DOOR_OPEN_CLOSED: Door open/closed boolean metric
 - BATTERY_VOLTAGE: Battery voltage metric
 - WEATHER: Weather (e.g. sunny, thunderstorms)
 - WIND_SPEED: Wind speed
 - WIND_DIRECTION: Wind direction
 - WIND_GUST: Wind gust
 - CO2: Carbon dioxide

@type.description:
A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized
protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least
one "/" character. The last segment of the URL's path must represent
the fully qualified name of the type (as in
`path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form
(e.g., leading "." is not accepted).

In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they
expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the
scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type
server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:

* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed.
* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a [google.protobuf.Type][]
  value in binary format, or produce an error.
* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the
  URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any
  lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved
  on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage
  breaking changes.)

Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official
protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with
type.googleapis.com.

Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be
used with implementation specific semantics.

ai_edited.description:
True when something non deterministic, in practice an LLM, produced or
changed this content. False when no AI did, which includes content a person
wrote and content a deterministic path produced. Absent when the origin was
not recorded. Do not report false in place of absent.

human_edited.description:
True when a person authored or changed this content. False when no person
did, which includes content a model generated and content a deterministic
path produced. Absent when the origin was not recorded. Do not report false
in place of absent.

s12.common.v1.AiMarking.description:
AiMarking carries the AI marking fact on an API representation, so a machine
can read whether AI and whether a person produced or changed the content.
It is the read side of the express path: one shared message with standard
property names, rather than every domain inventing its own field for the
same fact.

Both fields are presence tracked. The three states each carry a different
meaning and must not be collapsed:

  true    The actor named by the field produced or changed this content.
  false   The actor named by the field is known not to have produced or
          changed this content. It is a claim about that actor only.
  absent  We did not record the origin.

false is not evidence that a deterministic path produced the content. Known
human only content can read ai_edited false, and known AI only content can
read human_edited false. Set a field to false only when you know it is false.
Leave it absent when you do not, so a consumer relying on the API for their
own obligation can tell "not true" from "not recorded". EU AI Act Article
50(2), engineering approach page.

 - CATEGORY_USER_ACCESS_AS_REPORTER_WHEN_SITE_MEMBER: CATEGORY_USER_ACCESS_AS_REPORTER_WHEN_SITE_MEMBER the user will gain access to issues they report

s12.tasks.v1.TimelineItem.Type.description:
The type of the timeline item.

 - TIMELINE_ITEM_UNKNOWN: Removed fields related to the cancelled actions/issues integration
An unknown type of timeline item.
 - TASK_CREATED: A timeline item for the creation of an action.
 - TASK_TITLE_UPDATED: A timeline item indicating that the title of the task has been updated.
 - TASK_DESCRIPTION_UPDATED: A timeline item indicating that the task's description has been updated.
 - TASK_ASSIGNEE_ADDED: A timeline item indicating that an assignee has been added to the task.
 - TASK_ASSIGNEE_REMOVED: A timeline item indicating that an assignee has been removed from the
task.
 - TASK_DUE_AT_UPDATED: A timeline item indicating that the due date of the task has been
updated.
 - TASK_STATUS_UPDATED: A timeline item indicating that the status of the task has been updated.
 - TASK_PRIORITY_UPDATED: A timeline item indicating that the priority of the task has been
updated.
 - TASK_COMMENT_ADDED: A timeline item indicating that a comment has been added to the task.
 - TASK_IMAGE_UPLOADED: A timeline item indicating that an image was added to the task.
This field is deprecated, and was replaced by the `TASK_MEDIA_ADDED`
type. It is kept here to maintain backwards compatibility.

@deprecated use TASK_MEDIA_UPLOADED instead
 - TASK_SITE_UPDATED: A timeline item indicating that the folder (site) of the task has been
updated.
 - TASK_DELETED: A timeline item indicating that this task has been deleted.
 - TASK_CATEGORY_UPDATED: A timeline item indicating that the category of this task has been
updated. This type is only relevant to issues.
 - INCIDENT_CREATED: A timeline item for the creation of an issue.
 - TASK_NOTIFICATION_SENT: A timeline item indicating that a notification about this task has been
sent.
 - TASK_MEDIA_UPLOADED: A timeline item indicating that media has been added to this task.
 - TASK_ASSIGNEE_UPDATED: reserved 17, 18, 19;
17 - 19 reserved for the cancelled actions/issues integration feature.
A timeline item indicating that the assignee of this task has been
updated.
 - TASK_LOCATION_ADDED: A timeline item indicating the geolocation of this issue.
This type is only relevant to issues.
 - TASK_INSPECTION_COMPLETED: A timeline item indicating that an inspection that has been linked to an
issue has been completed. This type is only relevant to issues.
 - TASK_INSPECTION_DELETED: A timeline item indicating that an inspection that has been linked to an
issue has been deleted. This type is only relevant to issues.
 - TASK_INSPECTION_ADDED: A timeline item indicating that an inspection has been linked to an
issue. This type is only relevant to issues.
 - TASK_ANSWER_ADDED: A timeline item indicating that an issue's custom question has been
answered. This type is only relevant to issues.
 - TASK_ASSET_UPDATED: A timeline item indicating that an action has an asset updated
 - TASK_LABELS_UPDATED: A timeline item indicating that an action has labels updated
 - TASK_SCHEDULE_UPDATED: A timeline item indicating that the schedule that created this action was
updated.
 - INCIDENT_CHILD_CREATED: A timeline item indicating that an action has been created from an issue
 - TASK_CUSTOM_FIELD_UPDATED: A timeline item indicating that a custom field on this task was updated.
 - TASK_OCCURRED_AT_UPDATED: A timeline item indicating that occurred at date for the task has been
updated.
 - TASK_MEDIA_DELETED: A timeline item indicating that media has been deleted from this task.

@type.description:
A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized
protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least
one "/" character. The last segment of the URL's path must represent
the fully qualified name of the type (as in
`path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form
(e.g., leading "." is not accepted).

In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they
expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the
scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type
server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:

* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed.
* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a [google.protobuf.Type][]
  value in binary format, or produce an error.
* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the
  URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any
  lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved
  on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage
  breaking changes.)

Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official
protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with
type.googleapis.com.

Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be
used with implementation specific semantics.

template.description:
The draft content, in the same shape the published read returns.
TemplateDefinition.version is always empty here — it is a property of the
published state. Use GetTemplateDefinition for the published version.

revision.description:
Opaque concurrency token identifying the exact state of this draft. Pass
it back when mutating or publishing the draft to act only if nothing has
changed since this read.

Treat the value as opaque and compare it only for equality. It is not
comparable to `GetTemplateDefinitionResponse.version`.
Publishing or discarding the draft destroys it and invalidates the token.
Re-read the draft to get a current token.

delete.description: Delete the template's draft. The published template is untouched. Requires edit permission on the template and the draft's current revision token.

parameters.name: template_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier for the template whose draft should be discarded.

parameters.name: if_draft_revision_is
parameters.description:
Discard only if the draft is exactly at this revision, taken from a prior
read or mutation. Otherwise ABORTED / STALE_DRAFT_REVISION, with the
current token in the ErrorInfo metadata under `current_draft_revision`,
which is empty when the draft no longer exists.

Required, unlike on UpdateTemplateDraft, because a discard destroys work
and cannot be undone. The draft may hold someone else's unpublished edits,
so only a draft you have read can be discarded.

s12.templates.pub.integration.v1.SideEff.description: Change describes one change the server made.

SideEffectKind identifies what was changed. New kinds are added as new
values; a caller that does not recognize one still receives `message`.

 - SIDE_EFFECT_KIND_WEIGHTING_ZEROED: Item weightings were zeroed because scoring was turned off.

set_item_label.description: Sets the label of one item.

s12.templates.pub.integration.v1.Templat.description:
TemplateOperation is one mutation against a template draft. Exactly one field
must be set. Each field names the thing it changes.

item_id.description:
The unique identifier for the item whose label changes. An item_id the
draft does not contain returns `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

label.description:
The new label. An empty string clears it. Leading and trailing whitespace
is trimmed.

s12.templates.pub.integration.v1.Templat.description:
SetItemLabelOperation sets the label of one item in the draft.

The maximum length depends on the item's type. Exceeding it returns
`INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the limit that applied. Limits count characters,
not bytes.

description.description:
The new description. An empty string clears it. Leading and trailing
whitespace is trimmed. Counts characters, not bytes.

s12.templates.pub.integration.v1.Templat.description: SetTemplateDescriptionOperation sets the template's description.

name.description:
The new display name. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed.
Newlines are not accepted. Counts characters, not bytes.

s12.templates.pub.integration.v1.Templat.description: SetTemplateNameOperation sets the template's display name.

skip_completion_confirmation.description: Whether the completion confirmation dialog is skipped.

s12.templates.pub.integration.v1.Templat.description:
SetTemplateSettingOperation changes one named template setting, leaving
every other setting untouched. Change several settings by sending several
operations; the request is atomic regardless. Repeated assignments to the
same setting apply in order, so the last one wins.

operations.description:
The operations to apply, in order and atomically. Later operations see the
effects of earlier ones, and if any operation fails none are applied. The
draft is created from the published content when it does not exist.

if_draft_revision_is.description:
Apply only if the draft is exactly at this revision, taken from a prior
read or mutation. Otherwise ABORTED / STALE_DRAFT_REVISION, with the
current token in the ErrorInfo metadata under `current_draft_revision`,
which is empty when the draft no longer exists.

Omit to apply to the draft as it stands. Use this when the change must not
land on top of edits you have not seen.

s12.templates.pub.integration.v1.Templat.description: UpdateTemplateDraftRequest parameters for `rpc UpdateTemplateDraft`.

revision.description: Opaque concurrency token for the draft as it stands after this change.

previous_revision.description:
The revision these operations were applied on top of. Empty when this call
created the draft.

A template can be edited from more than one place at once. A person may be
in the web editor while an integration calls the API. When this differs
from the revision you last saw, another editor changed the draft in between
and your local copy is behind; refetch it. This is advisory and reported
after the fact. To refuse the write instead, send if_draft_revision_is.

@type.description:
A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized
protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least
one "/" character. The last segment of the URL's path must represent
the fully qualified name of the type (as in
`path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form
(e.g., leading "." is not accepted).

In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they
expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the
scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type
server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:

* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed.
* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a [google.protobuf.Type][]
  value in binary format, or produce an error.
* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the
  URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any
  lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved
  on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage
  breaking changes.)

Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official
protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with
type.googleapis.com.

Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be
used with implementation specific semantics.
